title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: CLYDE'S BOW
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Clyde Bascomb, a fifty-seven-year-old grain elevator operator from Wichita, Kansas.
Clyde honks at red lights. Before they turn green.
So for their thirtieth anniversary, his wife Nadine gave him a bow and arrow. And a warning.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BARN
segments.quote: He who wisheth one day to fly, must first learn standing and walking and running and climbing and dancing: one doth not fly into flying.
segments.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
lines: Nadine signed them up for the county's Thanksgiving Turkey Shoot, a charity contest.
At his first lesson, Clyde went straight for the far target. His arrow hit the barn.
His coach Ezra, a retired crop duster, pointed to a sign from the German thinker Friedrich Nietzsche:
He who wisheth one day to fly, must first learn standing and walking and running and climbing and dancing: one doth not fly into flying.
So Clyde spent two weeks shooting from five steps away. He felt silly. He got better.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE EYE
segments.quote: In the long run men hit only what they aim at.
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: The targets were paper turkeys. Clyde aimed at the whole bird, and his arrows went everywhere.
Ezra said, Henry David Thoreau put it best:
In the long run men hit only what they aim at.
So Clyde stopped aiming at the turkey and aimed at its tiny eye.
His arrows bunched up like they were waiting for a bus.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: ONE BREATH
segments.quote: Haste is always the parent of failure.
segments.author: Herodotus
lines: But Clyde shot the way he drove. Three arrows in ten seconds. Three misses.
Ezra quoted Herodotus, the old Greek historian:
Haste is always the parent of failure.
So Clyde learned one breath for every arrow. Breathe, pull, hold, let go.
He even tried it at red lights. The man behind him honked.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: NADINE
segments.quote: In jealousy there is more of self-love than love.
segments.author: François de La Rochefoucauld
lines: Then Nadine hit three turkey eyes in a row. Clyde blamed the wind, the sun, and her lucky socks.
Nadine smiled and read him a line from La Rochefoucauld, a French writer:
In jealousy there is more of self-love than love.
Ouch. So Clyde started cheering her good shots.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE WIND
segments.quote: We cannot direct the wind, but we can adjust the sails.
segments.author: Old saying
lines: On contest day, a Kansas wind blew thirty miles an hour. Everybody complained.
Ezra just grinned and said the old sailors' saying:
We cannot direct the wind, but we can adjust the sails.
Clyde aimed a hair into the wind, took one breath, and let go.
He and Nadine both made the final.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TURKEYS
segments.quote: Gratitude is the memory of the heart.
segments.author: Old French saying
lines: Nadine won. Clyde came second, by one point, and cheered the loudest.
They gave their prize turkeys to the food pantry, and bought twenty more.
The thank-you card had an old French saying:
Gratitude is the memory of the heart.
Now Clyde waits at green lights. When someone honks, he just waves.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start small. Aim small. Breathe. Cheer. Adjust. Be grateful.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start small. Aim at one small spot. Take a breath. Cheer, don't sulk. Adjust for the wind. And be grateful.
I tried archery once. The target was perfectly safe. The parking lot was not.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
